title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
prompt:
Given `points[i] = [xi, yi]`, the cost to connect two points is their Manhattan distance `|xi - xj| + |yi - yj|`. Return the minimum total cost to connect all points, so that there is exactly one path between any two.

**Example**: `[[0,0],[2,2],[3,10],[5,2],[7,0]]` → `20`.

**Constraints**: `1 <= points.length <= 1000`, coordinates within ±10⁶, all points distinct.
hints: 'Connect everything, exactly one path between any two, as cheaply as possible.' What is that structure called?
Build a minimum spanning tree. Grow it from one point, always adding the cheapest connection from the tree to a point not yet in it. Every pair of points is a possible edge.
Min-heap of `{cost, point}` starting with `{0, 0}`. Pop, skip if already in the tree, add its cost, then push `{manhattan(u, v), v}` for every point v not yet in the tree.

solution.explanation: Prim's algorithm is correct because the cheapest edge crossing from the tree to the rest of the points always belongs to some MST (the cut property). The graph is complete, so distances are computed as needed instead of stored, and repeat pops are skipped with `inMST`. O(n² log n) time, O(n²) heap space (an array-based Prim is O(n²) time, O(n) space).
